# Create Custom Genmoji and Images with Apple Intelligence

> **In short:** Apple Intelligence — Apple's built-in AI for iPhone, iPad and Mac — can turn a short description into a custom Genmoji emoji or a small illustrated image you can drop into Messages. You need a recent supported Apple device, the latest system update, and the feature turned on in Settings.

By the end of this guide, you'll be able to type a quick idea, watch Apple Intelligence draw it, and send it as a sticker or custom emoji in your next conversation. This is for anyone with a supported iPhone or iPad, an Apple ID signed in on the device, and a few minutes to try.

## Before you start

- **Device**: a recent iPhone or iPad that supports Apple Intelligence — Apple publishes the current list of supported models on its support page, since the requirements change with new releases. Older devices can't run these features.
- **Software**: the latest available system update for your device. To check, open **Settings → General → Software Update** and install anything waiting there. The exact version you need depends on your device and region.
- **Apple ID**: signed in on the device, with the region and language set to a country where Apple Intelligence is currently available. If you're not sure, US English is the broadest option.
- **Apple Intelligence setting**: turned on. It's included with supported devices at no extra cost, and the first time you switch it on the features may take a little while to appear in your apps.
- **Time**: about 5 minutes the first time, then under a minute once you know the flow.

## Step 1 — Turn on Apple Intelligence

Open the **Settings** app (the gray gear icon on your home screen) and scroll down to a section that includes the words **Apple Intelligence** — in current iOS versions it sits near the top, sometimes grouped with Siri in a combined entry. Tap into that section and look for a toggle or button to switch Apple Intelligence on. If you see wording about joining a waitlist or finishing setup, follow that prompt too — Apple activates new users in batches, so you may wait minutes or hours. While you wait, Genmoji and Image Playground won't yet appear in your apps, so this is a great moment to jot down a few ideas you'd love to try later.

💬 Example: while you wait, jot down three ideas like "sleepy sloth with coffee" or "your dog in a cape."

You'll know it worked when Settings shows a status line indicating Apple Intelligence is ready, or when you start seeing Apple Intelligence features appear in apps like Messages.

## Step 2 — Open Image Playground

You can start in two places. The first is a standalone **Image Playground** app — swipe down on your home screen to search for "Image Playground" and tap the result. The second is from inside Messages, Notes, or Freeform: tap the **+** or **Apps** icon next to the text field, then look for an Image Playground option in the menu. Both paths take you to a similar screen with a blank preview area at the top and a text box at the bottom prompting you to describe an image. The standalone app gives you more room to experiment, so it's the friendlier starting point. If neither option appears, your device or system version probably doesn't support Apple Intelligence — double-check the device list and the update from "Before you start."

💬 Example: open the standalone app first so you have a full canvas to play with.

You'll know it worked when you see an empty preview at the top and a text box at the bottom ready for your description.

## Step 3 — Type what you want to see

Tap the text box at the bottom of the screen and write a short, clear description of the picture you have in mind. A few specific details usually work better than a long paragraph — think of it as giving directions to a friend, not writing a novel. After a second or two, Apple Intelligence shows several preview images above the box, each with a slightly different look. To try new ideas, edit your words rather than starting over; the previews usually refresh in a couple of seconds. If the first results miss the mark, rephrase instead of regenerating — swapping one word often changes the whole image.

💬 Example: "a happy golden retriever wearing a tiny wizard hat, cartoon style."

You'll know it worked when you see at least one preview you actually like, even if it's not perfect yet.

## Step 4 — Choose a style and refine

Above the previews you should see style options — Apple's documentation lists styles such as **Animation** and **Illustration**, and your iOS version may show additional choices. Tap whichever options you see and watch the same idea take on a different look. Swipe through the previews to find a version you like, and tap a preview to open it full size. If the image is close but not quite right, change one or two words in your description — try swapping "happy" for "curious" or adding "with a red collar" — and watch the previews update. One honest note: Image Playground leans toward illustrated, stylized results. It can draft a fun image in seconds, but it can't make photorealistic photos or perfectly match every tiny detail you describe.

💬 Example: if "cartoon style" gives you a flat look, try adding "soft shading" or "bright background."

You'll know it worked when you find a preview you'd happily send to a friend.

## Step 5 — Save or share your image

When you have a preview you like, tap it to open the full version. From there, look for an option like **Done** or **Save** to keep it in your Image Playground library. To send it somewhere, tap the **Share** button — usually a square with an arrow pointing up — and choose where it should go: Messages, Mail, Notes, or any other app that accepts images. You may also see a **More** option for copying the image or saving it to your Photos library. Anything you create stays on your device by default, so feel free to experiment without worrying about your prompts being shared. If the Share menu doesn't show the app you want, save the image to Photos first and then insert it into your chat from there.

💬 Example: tap Share, choose Messages, pick a chat, hit Send, and your drawing arrives as a sticker-style image.

You'll know it worked when your image shows up in the conversation looking just like the preview.

## Step 6 — Make a custom Genmoji in Messages

Genmoji (a custom emoji made by Apple Intelligence) lives inside the Messages app. Open any conversation, tap the **emoji** button — the smiley face icon — in the text field, then look near the top of the emoji panel for something like a colorful Genmoji entry. Apple's design often uses a smiley face with a sparkle or glow, though the exact icon can vary by iOS version. Tap it, then type a description in the search bar. Apple Intelligence creates several custom emoji based on your words. Tap the one you like, and it sends just like a regular emoji. If you don't see a Genmoji option, your system software may be missing a recent Apple Intelligence update, or setup may still be finishing — check the Settings screen from Step 1 and install any pending system update.

💬 Example: type "sleepy sloth drinking coffee" — a perfect Monday morning chat reaction.

You'll know it worked when your custom emoji shows up in the message bubble, sized like any other emoji.

## Common mistakes

- **Writing a description that's too long.** A paragraph stuffed with adjectives confuses the tool and produces muddy results. Keep it under about 10 words — "robot painting a sunset" usually beats a longer, more detailed version.
- **Expecting a photorealistic photo.** Image Playground is designed for illustrated, friendly images, not camera-style pictures. If you want photo-style results, this isn't the right tool — try a different image generator instead.
- **Not seeing the Genmoji option in Messages.** Usually this means your system software is out of date, or Apple Intelligence is still finishing setup. Open Settings → General → Software Update, install the latest version your device offers, then re-check the Apple Intelligence screen from Step 1.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** send a one-of-a-kind "happy birthday" sticker to a friend, react to a group chat with a custom emoji no one else has, or make a quick visual for a family message — no design skills needed.
- **For your work or business:** sketch a concept for a slide or social post in seconds and drop it into a message or email as a quick visual aid when you don't have time to open a full design tool.
- **If you're just getting started:** try the Image Playground app first because the bigger canvas makes it easier to experiment, then move on to Genmoji in Messages once you feel comfortable.

## Try it now

Open Image Playground and type "pizza slice wearing sunglasses at the beach" — see what Apple Intelligence draws, then send it to your favorite chat and watch the reaction.
